items.title: Quiz Q#501 · William Cowper
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Cowper
items.stem: Which 1782 poetry collection marked William Cowper's first independent volume of verse, containing moral satires in heroic couplets such as 'Table Talk', 'The Progress of Error', and 'Expostulation'?
items.explanation: William Cowper's 'Poems' (1782) established his literary reputation, collecting eight substantial didactic poems in heroic couplets examining contemporary social morality and religious faith.

items.title: Quiz Q#502 · William Cowper
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Cowper
items.stem: In which landmark work by William Cowper does the character of The narrator (Cowper, telling the sailor's death and then reading his own life in it) appear?
items.explanation: The narrator is a prominent figure in William Cowper's The Castaway, characterized as cowper, telling the sailor's death and then reading his own life in it.

items.title: Quiz Q#503 · William Cowper
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Cowper
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Obscurest night involved the sky"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in William Cowper's The Castaway (1803).

items.title: Quiz Q#504 · William Cowper
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Cowper
items.stem: Which haunting 1799 lyric poem by William Cowper, based on an episode from George Anson’s voyage, parallels the physical drowning of an abandoned sailor with the poet’s own spiritual despair?
items.explanation: Written in March 1799 shortly before his death, Cowper's 'The Castaway' ends with the tragic realization: 'I beneath a rougher sea, / And whelm’d in deeper gulfs than he', mourning his conviction of eternal damnation.

items.title: Quiz Q#505 · Edward Gibbon
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Edward Gibbon
items.stem: In which landmark work by Edward Gibbon does the character of Edward Gibbon (The historian, speaking in his own ironic prose) appear?
options: Memoirs of My Life and Writings
The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
Essai sur l’Étude de la Littérature
items.explanation: Edward Gibbon is a prominent figure in Edward Gibbon's The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, characterized as the historian, speaking in his own ironic prose.

items.title: Quiz Q#506 · Edward Gibbon
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Edward Gibbon
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Revenge is profitable, gratitude is expensive"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Edward Gibbon's The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire (1776-1788).

items.title: Quiz Q#507 · Edward Gibbon
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Edward Gibbon
items.stem: Which monumental six-volume historical masterpiece published between 1776 and 1788 by Edward Gibbon traces Western civilization from the age of Trajan to the fall of Constantinople in 1453?
options: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
Memoirs of My Life and Writings
Essai sur l’Étude de la Littérature
items.explanation: Gibbon's 'The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire' (1776–1788) is acclaimed for its panoramic historical sweep, exhaustive use of primary sources, and biting ironic prose, particularly regarding early Christian controversies in Chapters 15 and 16.

items.title: Quiz Q#508 · Thomas Paine
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Thomas Paine
items.stem: In which landmark work by Thomas Paine does the character of Thomas Paine (The unnamed author, speaking as a plain citizen to the colonies) appear?
items.explanation: Thomas Paine is a prominent figure in Thomas Paine's Common Sense, characterized as the unnamed author, speaking as a plain citizen to the colonies.

items.title: Quiz Q#509 · Thomas Paine
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Thomas Paine
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Society is produced by our wants"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Thomas Paine's Common Sense (1776).

items.title: Quiz Q#510 · Thomas Paine
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Thomas Paine
items.stem: Which incendiary 48-page pamphlet published in Philadelphia in January 1776 by Thomas Paine used plain, direct prose to advocate immediate American independence and republican government?
items.explanation: Thomas Paine's 'Common Sense' (1776) sold hundreds of thousands of copies across the American colonies, dismantling the myth of benevolent British monarchy and galvanizing public support for the Declaration of Independence.

items.title: Quiz Q#511 · Thomas Paine
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Thomas Paine
items.stem: In which landmark work by Thomas Paine does the character of Thomas Paine (The author, answering Edmund Burke in his own voice) appear?
items.explanation: Thomas Paine is a prominent figure in Thomas Paine's Rights of Man, characterized as the author, answering edmund burke in his own voice.

items.title: Quiz Q#512 · Thomas Paine
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Thomas Paine
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"My country is the world"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Thomas Paine's Rights of Man (1791).

items.title: Quiz Q#513 · Thomas Paine
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Thomas Paine
items.stem: Which influential two-part political tract (1791–1792) by Thomas Paine defended the French Revolution against Edmund Burke and outlined early proposals for progressive taxation and a social safety net?
items.explanation: Thomas Paine's 'Rights of Man' asserted that human rights are inherent in nature rather than granted by government charters, leading to his indictment for seditious libel in Great Britain.

items.title: Quiz Q#514 · Thomas Paine
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Thomas Paine
items.stem: In which landmark work by Thomas Paine does the character of Thomas Paine (The author, stating his own faith and criticising churches) appear?
items.explanation: Thomas Paine is a prominent figure in Thomas Paine's Age of Reason, characterized as the author, stating his own faith and criticising churches.

items.title: Quiz Q#515 · Thomas Paine
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Thomas Paine
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"I believe in one God, and no more"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Thomas Paine's Age of Reason (1794).

items.title: Quiz Q#516 · Thomas Paine
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Thomas Paine
items.stem: Which controversial 1794–1795 theological work by Thomas Paine advocated Deism, challenged biblical inerrancy, and declared: 'My own mind is my own church'?
items.explanation: In 'The Age of Reason' (1794–1795), written in part during his imprisonment in Revolutionary France, Paine rejected institutional dogmas and biblical miracles in favor of a rational creator revealed through the natural order.

items.title: Quiz Q#517 · James Boswell
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · James Boswell
items.stem: In which landmark work by James Boswell does the character of James Boswell (The biographer and Johnson's younger friend) appear?

items.explanation: This famous line appears in James Boswell's The Life of Samuel Johnson (1791).

items.title: Quiz Q#519 · James Boswell
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · James Boswell
items.stem: Which celebrated 1791 biography by James Boswell revolutionized the genre through its dramatic dialogue, intimate personal anecdotes, and meticulous verbatim recording of Dr. Samuel Johnson’s conversations?
options: Journal of a Tour to the Hebrides
items.explanation: James Boswell's 'The Life of Samuel Johnson, LL.D.' (1791) is widely acclaimed as the greatest biography in English literature, immortalizing Johnson's wit, moral character, and literary circle.

items.title: Quiz Q#520 · James Boswell
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · James Boswell
items.stem: In which landmark work by James Boswell does the character of James Boswell (The Scottish host who keeps the diary) appear?
options: Journal of a Tour to the Hebrides
items.explanation: James Boswell is a prominent figure in James Boswell's Journal of a Tour to the Hebrides, characterized as the scottish host who keeps the diary.

items.title: Quiz Q#521 · James Boswell
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · James Boswell
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"The Journal of a Tour to the Hebrides"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in James Boswell's Journal of a Tour to the Hebrides (1785).

items.title: Quiz Q#522 · James Boswell
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · James Boswell
items.stem: Which 1785 travel journal by James Boswell records the autumn 1773 journey he undertook with Samuel Johnson through the Scottish Highlands and western islands?
options: Journal of a Tour to the Hebrides
items.explanation: Boswell's 'The Journal of a Tour to the Hebrides with Samuel Johnson, LL.D.' (1785) complemented Johnson's own travel book, offering lively, candid observations of Johnson interacting with Scottish Highland society.

items.title: Quiz Q#523 · George Crabbe
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · George Crabbe
items.stem: In which landmark work by George Crabbe does the character of The Speaker (A poet who rejects pretty lies about country life) appear?
items.explanation: The Speaker is a prominent figure in George Crabbe's The Village, characterized as a poet who rejects pretty lies about country life.

items.title: Quiz Q#524 · George Crabbe
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · George Crabbe
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"The village life, and every care that reigns"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in George Crabbe's The Village (1783).

items.title: Quiz Q#525 · George Crabbe
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · George Crabbe
items.stem: Which 1783 poem in heroic couplets by George Crabbe attacked romanticized pastoral idyllicism (such as Goldsmith's 'Sweet Auburn') by depicting the grim poverty, disease, and harsh labor of rural life?
items.explanation: In 'The Village' (1783), written with the encouragement of Samuel Johnson, Crabbe famously declared: 'I paint the cot, / As Truth will paint it, and as Bards will not', offering stark social realism.

items.title: Quiz Q#526 · Olaudah Equiano
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Olaudah Equiano

options: The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano
items.explanation: Olaudah Equiano is a prominent figure in Olaudah Equiano's The Interesting Narrative, characterized as the narrator, also called gustavus vassa, who tells his own life.

items.title: Quiz Q#527 · Olaudah Equiano
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Olaudah Equiano
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"O, ye nominal Christians!"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Olaudah Equiano's The Interesting Narrative (1789).

items.title: Quiz Q#528 · Olaudah Equiano
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Olaudah Equiano
items.stem: Which groundbreaking 1789 autobiography by Olaudah Equiano (Gustavus Vassa) provided a firsthand account of the Middle Passage and became a powerful instrument in the British abolitionist movement?
options: The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano
items.explanation: Olaudah Equiano's 'The Interesting Narrative' (1789) is a foundational text of Black Atlantic and Anglophone literature, detailing his Igbo childhood, brutal enslavement, conversion to Christianity, and purchase of his freedom.

items.title: Quiz Q#529 · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.stem: In which landmark work by Richard Brinsley Sheridan does the character of Captain Jack Absolute (Sir Anthony's son, who pretends to be poor Ensign Beverley) appear?
items.explanation: Captain Jack Absolute is a prominent figure in Richard Brinsley Sheridan's The Rivals, characterized as sir anthony's son, who pretends to be poor ensign beverley.

items.title: Quiz Q#530 · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"He is the very pineapple of politeness"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Richard Brinsley Sheridan's The Rivals (1775).

items.title: Quiz Q#531 · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.stem: Which 1775 comedy of manners by Richard Brinsley Sheridan, set in fashionable Bath, introduced the sentimental Lydia Languish, Captain Absolute disguised as Ensign Beverley, and Mrs. Malaprop?
items.explanation: Sheridan's 'The Rivals' (1775) delighted London audiences with its witty ridicule of sentimental romantic illusions and immortalized the linguistic blunder 'malapropism' through Mrs. Malaprop's verbal mix-ups.

items.title: Quiz Q#532 · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.stem: In which landmark work by Richard Brinsley Sheridan does the character of Lady Sneerwell (The hostess whose circle lives on scandal) appear?
items.explanation: Lady Sneerwell is a prominent figure in Richard Brinsley Sheridan's The School for Scandal, characterized as the hostess whose circle lives on scandal.

items.title: Quiz Q#533 · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Here's to the maiden of bashful fifteen"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Richard Brinsley Sheridan's The School for Scandal (1777).

items.title: Quiz Q#534 · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.stem: Which 1777 masterpiece of dramatic wit by Richard Brinsley Sheridan satirizes malicious gossipmongers through the contrasting brothers Charles and Joseph Surface, featuring the famous 'screen scene'?
items.explanation: Sheridan's 'The School for Scandal' (1777) is considered the peak of 18th-century comedy, contrasting the true benevolence of the spendthrift Charles Surface with the hypocritical 'sentiments' of his treacherous brother Joseph.

items.title: Quiz Q#535 · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.stem: In which landmark work by Richard Brinsley Sheridan does the character of Puff (A professional praiser who has written a tragedy) appear?
items.explanation: Puff is a prominent figure in Richard Brinsley Sheridan's The Critic, characterized as a professional praiser who has written a tragedy.

items.title: Quiz Q#536 · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Enter Tilburina stark mad in white satin"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Richard Brinsley Sheridan's The Critic (1779).

items.title: Quiz Q#537 · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.stem: Which 1779 theatrical burlesque by Richard Brinsley Sheridan, modeled on Buckingham’s 'The Rehearsal', parodies melodramatic stage tragedies through the disastrous rehearsal of Mr. Puff’s 'The Spanish Armada'?
items.explanation: Sheridan's 'The Critic: or, A Tragedy Rehearsed' (1779) satirizes theatrical vanity and literary criticism through the characters of Mr. Puff, Sir Fretful Plagiary, and the critics Sneer and Dangle.

items.title: Quiz Q#538 · Fanny Burney
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Fanny Burney
items.stem: In which landmark work by Fanny Burney does the character of Evelina Anville (The young heroine whose letters tell most of the story) appear?
items.explanation: Evelina Anville is a prominent figure in Fanny Burney's Evelina, characterized as the young heroine whose letters tell most of the story.

items.title: Quiz Q#539 · Fanny Burney
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Fanny Burney
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"The child of his heart"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Fanny Burney's Evelina (1778).

items.title: Quiz Q#540 · Fanny Burney
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Fanny Burney
items.stem: Which 1778 epistolary novel published anonymously by Fanny Burney, subtitled 'The History of a Young Lady’s Entrance into the World', follows an innocent provincial heroine navigating London high society and vulgar relatives?
items.explanation: Fanny Burney's 'Evelina' (1778) established the female novel of manners, paving the way for Jane Austen by combining keen social comedy with heroine Evelina Anville's courtship with Lord Orville.

items.title: Quiz Q#541 · Fanny Burney
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Fanny Burney

items.explanation: Cecilia Beverley is a prominent figure in Fanny Burney's Cecilia, characterized as the heiress whose fortune depends on a name clause.

items.title: Quiz Q#542 · Fanny Burney
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Fanny Burney
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"The result of pride and prejudice"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Fanny Burney's Cecilia (1782).

items.title: Quiz Q#543 · Fanny Burney
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Fanny Burney
items.stem: Which 1782 novel by Fanny Burney follows a wealthy heiress forbidden by her uncle’s will from marrying unless her husband adopts her surname, providing the final phrase that inspired the title 'Pride and Prejudice'?
items.explanation: Burney's 'Cecilia, or Memoirs of an Heiress' (1782) closes with a famous passage stating the catastrophe was brought about by 'PRIDE and PREJUDICE', which Jane Austen later adapted for her own title.

items.title: Quiz Q#544 · Fanny Burney
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Fanny Burney
items.stem: In which landmark work by Fanny Burney does the character of Camilla Tyrold (The young heroine whose errors delay her happiness) appear?
items.explanation: Camilla Tyrold is a prominent figure in Fanny Burney's Camilla, characterized as the young heroine whose errors delay her happiness.

items.title: Quiz Q#545 · Fanny Burney
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Fanny Burney
items.stem: Which 1796 novel by Fanny Burney, subtitled 'A Picture of Youth', examines the perils of debt, reputation, and romantic misunderstandings among the Tyrold sisters, purchased by subscription by Jane Austen?
items.explanation: Fanny Burney's 'Camilla' (1796) explores female financial vulnerability and moral guidance through the romance of Camilla Tyrold and Edgar Mandelbert, proving immensely successful in late-18th-century England.

items.title: Quiz Q#546 · Fanny Burney
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Fanny Burney
items.stem: In which landmark work by Fanny Burney does the character of Juliet Granville (The nameless heroine, later known as the Earl of Granville's daughter) appear?
items.explanation: Juliet Granville is a prominent figure in Fanny Burney's The Wanderer, characterized as the nameless heroine, later known as the earl of granville's daughter.

items.title: Quiz Q#547 · Fanny Burney
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Fanny Burney
items.stem: Which 1814 novel by Fanny Burney, subtitled 'Female Difficulties', portrays the desperate economic and social struggles of an incognito French émigrée seeking independent livelihoods in England during the French Revolution?
items.explanation: Burney's final novel 'The Wanderer' (1814) presents a searing analysis of the lack of respectable economic opportunities available to impoverished women in late-18th-century society.

items.title: Quiz Q#550 · Thomas Chatterton
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Thomas Chatterton
items.stem: Which celebrated body of pseudo-medieval poems in antique spelling, circulated in manuscript by Thomas Chatterton before his suicide in 1770, was later published in 1777 by Thomas Tyrwhitt?

Rowley poems circulated before his death
The Execution of Sir Charles Bawdin
items.explanation: Chatterton's pseudo-medieval Rowley manuscripts circulated among Bristol antiquarians before his death, later sparking intense literary debate among scholars like Tyrwhitt and Warton.

items.title: Quiz Q#553 · Thomas Chatterton
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Thomas Chatterton
items.stem: Which famous 1777 posthumous collection of poems, composed in pseudo-archaic 15th-century English, was fabricated by the teenage poet Thomas Chatterton and attributed to a fictional medieval monk?
options: Rowley poems circulated before his death
Poems, Supposed to Have Been Written at Bristol, by Thomas Rowley
The Execution of Sir Charles Bawdin
items.explanation: Thomas Chatterton attributed his forged medieval poems to the fictional 15th-century monk Thomas Rowley; following his suicide at age 17 in 1770, he became an iconic tragic martyr of poetic genius for the Romantics.

Rowley poems circulated before his death
items.explanation: Thomas Chatterton is a prominent figure in Thomas Chatterton's Rowley poems circulated before his death, characterized as the living boy who passed the poems off as old manuscripts.

items.title: Quiz Q#556 · Phillis Wheatley

Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"'Twas mercy brought me from my Pagan land"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Phillis Wheatley's Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral (1773).

items.title: Quiz Q#557 · Phillis Wheatley
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Phillis Wheatley
items.stem: Which landmark 1773 collection of poems published in London made its author the first African American and only the second woman in colonial America to publish a book of poetry?
options: Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral
On Being Brought from Africa to America
items.explanation: Phillis Wheatley's 'Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral' (1773) demonstrated extraordinary mastery of Augustan heroic couplets, Miltonic allusions, and subtle critiques of slavery.

items.explanation: William Godwin's 'Caleb Williams' (1794) is an early psychological thriller illustrating how the legal and social power of the aristocracy corrupts justice and crushes the innocent.

items.title: Quiz Q#564 · William Godwin

"Enquiry, and the improvement of the human mind"

items.title: Quiz Q#567 · William Godwin

items.stem: Which monumental 1793 philosophical work by William Godwin rejected all government institutions, law, and marriage in favor of absolute reason, benevolence, and human perfectibility?
options: or, The Adventures of Caleb Williams
items.explanation: Godwin's 'Political Justice' (1793) was the foundational text of philosophical anarchism, profoundly inspiring the young Wordsworth, Coleridge, and especially Percy Bysshe Shelley.

items.title: Quiz Q#568 · William Godwin
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Godwin
items.stem: In which landmark work by William Godwin does the character of William Godwin (The narrator and widower, writing a candid life) appear?
options: Memoirs of the Author of A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
or, The Adventures of Caleb Williams
items.explanation: William Godwin is a prominent figure in William Godwin's Memoirs of the Author of A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, characterized as the narrator and widower, writing a candid life.

items.title: Quiz Q#569 · William Godwin
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Godwin
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"A sympathy in their excellencies"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in William Godwin's Memoirs of the Author of A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1798).

items.title: Quiz Q#570 · William Godwin
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Godwin
items.stem: Which candid 1798 biographical memoir by William Godwin recounted the life, unorthodox romances, and suicide attempts of his late wife Mary Wollstonecraft?
options: or, The Adventures of Caleb Williams
Memoirs of the Author of A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
items.explanation: William Godwin published 'Memoirs of the Author of A Vindication of the Rights of Woman' in 1798 with frank honesty, which inadvertently sparked conservative scandal and damaged Wollstonecraft's contemporary reputation.

items.title: Quiz Q#571 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"How sweet I roam'd from field to field"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in William Blake's Poetical Sketches (1783).

items.title: Quiz Q#572 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem: Which 1783 volume of juvenile lyrics and dramatic fragments was the only work by William Blake printed by letterpress typography during his lifetime without illuminated engravings?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
items.explanation: Privately printed for friends in 1783, 'Poetical Sketches' contains Blake's earliest lyric poetry, experimenting with Elizabethan and Spenserian forms before he developed illuminated printing.

items.title: Quiz Q#573 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem: In which landmark work by William Blake does the character of The Piper (The singer of the Introduction, who writes happy songs for a child) appear?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
items.explanation: The Piper is a prominent figure in William Blake's Songs of Innocence, characterized as the singer of the introduction, who writes happy songs for a child.

items.title: Quiz Q#574 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Little Lamb who made thee"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in William Blake's Songs of Innocence (1789).

items.title: Quiz Q#575 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem: Which 1789 illuminated collection of nineteen lyric poems by William Blake presents a pastoral vision of childhood, spiritual purity, and divine love through speakers like the Piper and the Lamb?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
items.explanation: William Blake's 'Songs of Innocence' (1789) etched text and illustrations together onto copper plates, presenting a harmonious pastoral vision of creation that he would later contrast with 'Songs of Experience'.

items.title: Quiz Q#576 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem: In which landmark work by William Blake does the character of The speaker (Blake's prophetic voice, who visits Hell and records its proverbs) appear?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
items.explanation: The speaker is a prominent figure in William Blake's The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, characterized as blake's prophetic voice, who visits hell and records its proverbs.

items.title: Quiz Q#577 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Without Contraries is no progression"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in William Blake's The Marriage of Heaven and Hell (1790).

items.title: Quiz Q#578 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem: Which 1790 illuminated book by William Blake subverts Swedenborgian mysticism and orthodox morality through aphoristic proverbs, declaring that 'Without Contraries is no progression' and praising Milton as a true poet of the Devil's party?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
items.explanation: Blake's 'The Marriage of Heaven and Hell' (1790) includes the famous 'Proverbs of Hell', celebrating energy, desire, and imagination against passive institutional restraint.

items.title: Quiz Q#579 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem: In which landmark work by William Blake does the character of The Bard (The prophet speaker of the Introduction) appear?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
items.explanation: The Bard is a prominent figure in William Blake's Songs of Experience, characterized as the prophet speaker of the introduction.

items.title: Quiz Q#580 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Tyger Tyger, burning bright"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in William Blake's Songs of Experience (1794).

items.title: Quiz Q#581 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem: Which 1794 illuminated collection by William Blake answers his earlier pastoral lyrics by exposing social exploitation, institutional cruelty, and spiritual repression through poems like 'The Tyger' and 'London'?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
items.explanation: In 'Songs of Experience' (1794), Blake examines human suffering under church, state, and industrial oppression, introducing the prophetic Bard who summons the fallen soul to awaken.

items.title: Quiz Q#582 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem: In which landmark work by William Blake does the character of The Piper (The singer of the Innocence introduction) appear?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
Songs of Innocence and of Experience
items.explanation: The Piper is a prominent figure in William Blake's Songs of Innocence and of Experience, characterized as the singer of the innocence introduction.

items.title: Quiz Q#583 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem: Which combined 1794 illuminated masterwork by William Blake carries the subtitle 'Shewing the Two Contrary States of the Human Soul', pairing complementary poems across childhood and adulthood?
options: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
items.explanation: Blake united both collections in 1794 to illustrate how spiritual maturity requires passing through innocence and experience, featuring paired contrasts such as 'The Lamb' and 'The Tyger'.

items.title: Quiz Q#584 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem: In which landmark work by William Blake does the character of Urizen (The Zoa of reason, often a tyrant maker of laws) appear?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
items.explanation: Urizen is a prominent figure in William Blake's The Four Zoas, characterized as the zoa of reason, often a tyrant maker of laws.

items.title: Quiz Q#585 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"What is the price of Experience?"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in William Blake's The Four Zoas (1893).

items.title: Quiz Q#586 · William Blake
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · William Blake
items.stem: Which sprawling, unfinished prophetic manuscript poem divided into nine 'Nights' by William Blake dramatizes the cosmic fall and division of the primordial Giant Albion into Urizen, Luvah, Tharmas, and Urthona?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
items.explanation: Written on proofs of Edward Young's 'Night Thoughts' between 1797 and 1807, Blake's 'The Four Zoas' represents his most ambitious mythological epic, remaining unpublished until W. B. Yeats and Edwin Ellis edited it in 1893.

items.title: Quiz Q#587 · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.stem: In which landmark work by Mary Wollstonecraft does the character of Mary Wollstonecraft (The writer, answering Burke in the form of a public letter) appear?
options: A Vindication of the Rights of Men
A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
Maria, or The Wrongs of Woman
Thoughts on the Education of Daughters
items.explanation: Mary Wollstonecraft is a prominent figure in Mary Wollstonecraft's A Vindication of the Rights of Men, characterized as the writer, answering burke in the form of a public letter.

items.title: Quiz Q#588 · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Virtue can only flourish amongst equals"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Mary Wollstonecraft's A Vindication of the Rights of Men (1790).

items.title: Quiz Q#589 · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.stem: Which passionate 1790 pamphlet by Mary Wollstonecraft, written in response to Edmund Burke’s 'Reflections', was the very first published rebuttal in the famous British Revolutionary Controversy?
options: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
Maria, or The Wrongs of Woman
A Vindication of the Rights of Men
Thoughts on the Education of Daughters
items.explanation: Published anonymously in November 1790 and under her own name in the second edition, Wollstonecraft's 'A Vindication of the Rights of Men' attacked aristocratic privilege, the slave trade, and Burke's sentimental defense of chivalry.

items.title: Quiz Q#590 · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.stem: In which landmark work by Mary Wollstonecraft does the character of Mary Wollstonecraft (The author, arguing that women are rational human beings) appear?
options: A Vindication of the Rights of Men
Maria, or The Wrongs of Woman
Thoughts on the Education of Daughters
A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
items.explanation: Mary Wollstonecraft is a prominent figure in Mary Wollstonecraft's A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, characterized as the author, arguing that women are rational human beings.

items.title: Quiz Q#591 · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Truth must be common to all"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Mary Wollstonecraft's A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792).

items.title: Quiz Q#592 · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.stem: Which foundational 1792 feminist treatise by Mary Wollstonecraft argued that women’s apparent intellectual deficiencies stem from inadequate education and demanded equal educational rights for women as rational human beings?
options: A Vindication of the Rights of Men
A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
Maria, or The Wrongs of Woman
Thoughts on the Education of Daughters
items.explanation: Mary Wollstonecraft's 'A Vindication of the Rights of Woman' (1792) critiqued Rousseau and educational conduct-books, insisting that women must cultivate reason to become virtuous citizens and equal companions to men.

items.title: Quiz Q#593 · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.stem: In which landmark work by Mary Wollstonecraft does the character of Maria Venables (The heroine, imprisoned by her husband though she is sane) appear?
options: A Vindication of the Rights of Men
A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
Maria, or The Wrongs of Woman
Thoughts on the Education of Daughters
items.explanation: Maria Venables is a prominent figure in Mary Wollstonecraft's Maria, or The Wrongs of Woman, characterized as the heroine, imprisoned by her husband though she is sane.

items.title: Quiz Q#594 · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"The misery and oppression, peculiar to women"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Mary Wollstonecraft's Maria, or The Wrongs of Woman (1798).

items.title: Quiz Q#595 · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Mary Wollstonecraft
items.stem: Which unfinished 1798 novel by Mary Wollstonecraft, published posthumously by William Godwin, portrays a woman imprisoned in a private insane asylum by her abusive husband to seize her property?
options: Maria, or The Wrongs of Woman
A Vindication of the Rights of Men
A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
Thoughts on the Education of Daughters
items.explanation: Wollstonecraft's 'Maria: or, The Wrongs of Woman' (1798) exposed the legal and social helplessness of women under 18th-century marriage laws, famously dramatizing cross-class solidarity between Maria and her working-class warder Jemima.

items.title: Quiz Q#596 · Robert Burns
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Robert Burns
items.stem: In which landmark work by Robert Burns does the character of The poet speaker (Burns, speaking as a farmer poet to mice, friends, and readers) appear?
options: Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect
items.explanation: The poet speaker is a prominent figure in Robert Burns's Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect, characterized as burns, speaking as a farmer poet to mice, friends, and readers.

items.title: Quiz Q#597 · Robert Burns
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Robert Burns
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"The best laid schemes o' Mice an' Men"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Robert Burns's Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect (1786).

items.title: Quiz Q#598 · Robert Burns
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Robert Burns
items.stem: Which historic 1786 volume printed at Kilmarnock established Robert Burns’s fame overnight as the 'Heaven-taught ploughman', containing masterpieces like 'To a Mouse' and 'The Cotter’s Saturday Night'?
options: Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect
items.explanation: Robert Burns's 'Kilmarnock edition' (1786) revitalized Scots vernacular poetry, employing the traditional Standard Habbie stanza to capture rural Scottish life, satirical wit, and compassionate egalitarianism.

items.title: Quiz Q#599 · Robert Burns
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Robert Burns
items.stem: In which landmark work by Robert Burns does the character of Tam o' Shanter (A farmer who drinks too long and then rides home) appear?
options: Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect
items.explanation: Tam o' Shanter is a prominent figure in Robert Burns's Tam o’ Shanter, characterized as a farmer who drinks too long and then rides home.

items.title: Quiz Q#600 · Robert Burns
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Robert Burns
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Kings may be blest, but Tam was glorious"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Robert Burns's Tam o’ Shanter (1791).

items.title: Quiz Q#601 · Robert Burns
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Robert Burns
items.stem: Which 1791 narrative comic masterpiece in rhyming octosyllabic couplets by Robert Burns follows an inebriated farmer who stumbles upon a witches’ coven at Alloway Kirk and flees on his mare Meg?
options: Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect
items.explanation: Robert Burns's 'Tam o' Shanter' (1791) is a tour de force of comic supernatural folklore, famous for the witches' dance, Nannie in her cutty sark, and Meg losing her tail at the Brig o' Doon.

items.title: Quiz Q#602 · Robert Burns
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Robert Burns
items.stem: In which landmark work by Robert Burns does the character of The poet speaker (Burns, now writing for a national Scottish audience) appear?
options: Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect
items.explanation: The poet speaker is a prominent figure in Robert Burns's Edinburgh edition, characterized as burns, now writing for a national scottish audience.

items.title: Quiz Q#603 · Robert Burns
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Robert Burns
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Fair fa' your honest, sonsie face"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Robert Burns's Edinburgh edition (1787).

items.title: Quiz Q#604 · Robert Burns
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Robert Burns
items.stem: Which 1787 expanded edition of Robert Burns's poems, published by William Creech following the poet’s celebrated winter in Edinburgh, introduced his verses to a wider British and international audience?
options: Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect
items.explanation: Following the sensational success of the 1786 Kilmarnock edition, the 1787 'Edinburgh edition' of 'Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect' doubled Burns's published poems and contained the famous frontispiece portrait painted by Alexander Nasmyth.

items.title: Quiz Q#605 · Ann Radcliffe
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Ann Radcliffe
items.stem: In which landmark work by Ann Radcliffe does the character of Adeline (The heroine, later revealed as the daughter of the murdered marquis) appear?
items.explanation: Adeline is a prominent figure in Ann Radcliffe's The Romance of the Forest, characterized as the heroine, later revealed as the daughter of the murdered marquis.

items.title: Quiz Q#606 · Ann Radcliffe
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Ann Radcliffe
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"If you wish to save your life"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Ann Radcliffe's The Romance of the Forest (1791).

items.title: Quiz Q#607 · Ann Radcliffe
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Ann Radcliffe
items.stem: Which 1791 Gothic novel by Ann Radcliffe established her literary reputation, following the persecuted heroine Adeline through the ruined abbey of St. Clair under the villainous Marquis de Montalt?
items.explanation: Ann Radcliffe's 'The Romance of the Forest' (1791) solidified her mastery of picturesque landscape description, suspense, and the technique of the explained supernatural.

items.title: Quiz Q#608 · Ann Radcliffe
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Ann Radcliffe
items.stem: In which landmark work by Ann Radcliffe does the character of Emily St Aubert (The orphan heroine who must keep her courage and her property) appear?
items.explanation: Emily St Aubert is a prominent figure in Ann Radcliffe's The Mysteries of Udolpho, characterized as the orphan heroine who must keep her courage and her property.

items.title: Quiz Q#609 · Ann Radcliffe
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Ann Radcliffe
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"Fate sits on these dark battlements, and frowns"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Ann Radcliffe's The Mysteries of Udolpho (1794).

items.title: Quiz Q#610 · Ann Radcliffe
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Ann Radcliffe
items.stem: Which archetypal 1794 Gothic romance by Ann Radcliffe follows Emily St. Aubert imprisoned in a sinister Apennine fortress by the ruthless Italian villain Montoni, famous for the mystery of the black veil?
items.explanation: Radcliffe's 'The Mysteries of Udolpho' (1794) is the defining Gothic romance of the 1790s, celebrated for its sublime mountain landscapes, terrifying suspense, and rational explanations for seemingly ghostly horrors.

items.title: Quiz Q#611 · Ann Radcliffe
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Ann Radcliffe
items.stem: In which landmark work by Ann Radcliffe does the character of Vincentio di Vivaldi (A young nobleman of Naples who loves Ellena) appear?
items.explanation: Vincentio di Vivaldi is a prominent figure in Ann Radcliffe's The Italian, characterized as a young nobleman of naples who loves ellena.

items.title: Quiz Q#612 · Ann Radcliffe
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Ann Radcliffe
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line or critical statement?
"He listened in deep attention"
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Ann Radcliffe's The Italian (1797).

items.title: Quiz Q#613 · Ann Radcliffe
items.meta: The Long Eighteenth Century · Ann Radcliffe
items.stem: Which powerful 1797 Gothic novel by Ann Radcliffe, written partly in response to Matthew Lewis’s 'The Monk', features the sinister monk Father Schedoni plotting against the young lovers Vincentio di Vivaldi and Ellena Rosalba?
items.explanation: In 'The Italian, or the Confessional of the Black Penitents' (1797), Radcliffe created one of the greatest Gothic villains in Father Schedoni, exploring the horrors of the Roman Inquisition with dramatic psychological depth.
